target.detail: the knock-off stall and the lock-up behind it

setup: Tick logos close enough to fool a birthday present, boxed trainers that were never near the real factory, a lock-up full of it out the back.
on_success: Move the lot to the market boys at a mark-up they can still triple. Everyone down the line thinks they got a deal.
on_fail: Trading Standards did a quiet visit last week and left a friend behind. The 'buyer' has a lanyard under his coat.
on_crit: A container's worth clears in an afternoon — a stag do, a market, and a bloke who 'supplies shops'.

target.name: match day
target.detail: the fake kits outside the ground

setup: Home game, thousands walking to the ground, half of them wanting this season's shirt at a quarter of the club shop. You have this season's shirt. Sort of.
on_success: Sell out before kickoff from a holdall and a folding table that vanishes when a steward looks over.
on_fail: Club's own stewards clock the pitch and the printing's off on the sponsor. A copper on horseback takes an interest.
on_crit: An away coach empties out and buys the lot for the trip home. Bulk, cash, gone before the whistle.

target.detail: the fake kits going out of a holdall outside the ground

setup: Home game, thousands walking to the ground, half of them wanting this season's shirt at a quarter of the club-shop price. You've got this season's shirt. The sponsor's printed a shade off, but nobody's looking that hard on the way in.
on_success: Sold out before kickoff from a holdall and a folding table that folds itself the second a steward looks over. Everyone thinks they got a deal.
on_fail: The club's own stewards clock the pitch, the printing's wrong on the badge, and a copper on a horse takes a slow interest in your table.
on_crit: An away coach empties out and buys the entire holdall for the trip home. Bulk, cash, gone before the whistle.

target.name: Baz
target.detail: the lock-up of boxed trainers that were never near the factory

setup: Tick logos close enough to fool a birthday present, boxes printed off the same machine as the shoes, and a lock-up out the back of the market stacked to the shutter.
on_success: Move the lot to the market boys at a mark-up they can still triple. Everyone down the line believes they're the clever one.
on_fail: Trading Standards did a quiet walk-round last week and left a friend behind, and your 'customer' has a lanyard under his coat.
on_crit: A container's worth clears in an afternoon — a stag do, a car boot, and a bloke who 'supplies shops' and doesn't blink at the price.

target.detail: the pop-up table of designer scent that smells almost right

setup: Christmas precinct, a table of boxed perfume with the names spelled just close enough, and a script about a warehouse clearance that people want to believe because the alternative is paying full price.
on_success: It smells nearly like the real thing for nearly an hour, which is exactly as long as anyone's checking. Cash box full by lunch.
on_fail: A woman sprays a tester, pulls a face she can't hide, and says the word 'fake' loud enough that the whole precinct turns round.

target.detail: the burned box sets going round the pubs in a sports bag

setup: A sports bag of copied box sets and the latest films that are still in the cinema, doing the rounds of the estate pubs on a Friday where the lighting's kind and the standards are low.
on_success: A tenner for a film nobody can see yet, three for twenty-five, and a whole pub that'd rather not ask how you've got it.
on_fail: One of them plays it back at home and it's a shaky cam with someone's head in the corner, and he wants his tenner back with interest.

target.name: Kel
target.detail: the phone-bits stall where nothing's genuine

setup: Market stall of chargers, cables and cases, all of it moulded in a shed and none of it safe, priced so low that the danger reads as a bargain to anyone in a hurry.
on_success: They sell faster than the real ones because they're a third of the price, and the burn risk is next month's problem for somebody who isn't you.
on_fail: One of last week's chargers has melted into somebody's socket and they've brought the blackened lump back to the stall in front of everyone.

target.detail: the cash-and-carry that stocks its shelves with your gear

setup: A back-street cash-and-carry that fills its shelves with knock-off razors, batteries and washing tabs, and a manager who buys by the pallet and asks nothing as long as the box says a brand.
on_success: A pallet of fake razors that shave nobody well moves in one go, and it's on a corner-shop shelf three counties over by the weekend.
on_fail: The manager's had a visit from a brand-protection firm with real lawyers and he's decided the safest pallet is the one he grasses up.

target.name: Farah
target.detail: the 'sample sale' of dresses copied from a catalogue

setup: An upstairs room done out like a boutique, a rail of wedding dresses stitched from photos of the real ones, and brides-to-be who want the dream for a tenth and won't look too close in the flattering light.
on_success: She cries, she pays, everyone's happy, and the dress holds together for exactly one perfect day, which is genuinely all it needs to.
on_fail: A mother-of-the-bride who does sewing spots a seam no real designer would allow and asks, very calmly, to speak to whoever's in charge.

target.detail: the pad of scratchcards that never had a winner in it

setup: A pub, a laminated pad of homemade scratchcards, a story about a raffle for a lad who's poorly. Every card's a pound, the top prize is real to nobody, and a full pub wants to feel generous.
on_success: Fifty quid off a room full of people who think they've done a good deed. The poorly lad is you, in a way, if you squint.
on_fail: Somebody actually knows the family you named and knows the lad's fine, and asks the question you have no answer to.
